name: Your CRM Sync and AI Automation Hub

parameters.content:
## 1 - CATCH THE CRM EVENT, PARK BAD DATA

HubSpot is shown as the example CRM, any CRM swaps in at the first node and the write-back. Every event is mapped into one standard record, and anything missing or malformed waits in a review table with the exact field named.

nodes.name: Section - 1 - CATCH THE CRM EVENT, PARK BAD DATA

parameters.content:
## 2 - RUN EACH EVENT ONCE, ANSWER THE CRM FAST

CRMs resend webhooks, so every event id is claimed once in a ledger and a repeat stops cold. The CRM gets its answer in milliseconds while the real work carries on behind it.

nodes.name: Section - 2 - RUN EACH EVENT ONCE, ANSWER THE CRM FAST

parameters.content:
## 3 - CLAUDE SHAPES IT, EVERY SYSTEM GETS ITS COPY

Claude cleans the names, maps the plan to invoice terms and writes the team summary, into a fixed schema. Ids and amounts come straight from the CRM, never from the model. A throttled call backs off and tries again.

nodes.name: Section - 3 - CLAUDE SHAPES IT, EVERY SYSTEM GETS ITS COPY

parameters.content:
## 4 - WRITE IT BACK TO THE CRM, CLOSE THE LOOP

The rep sees the invoice number, ops record and sync time on the deal itself. The ledger row holds every id that was created, so any sync can be traced in one lookup.

nodes.name: Section - 4 - WRITE IT BACK TO THE CRM, CLOSE THE LOOP

parameters.content:
## 5 - NOTHING FAILS QUIETLY

One error trigger covers every step. The event is marked failed with its payload kept, and the team gets the deal, the step that broke and a link to the run, ready to replay.

nodes.name: Section - 5 - NOTHING FAILS QUIETLY
1 - HubSpot or Your CRM: Deal Moved to Closed Won
nodes.notes: HubSpot here as the example. Salesforce, Pipedrive, Zoho or GoHighLevel plug into this same spot.

nodes.name: 2 - Normalize and Validate Into One Standard Record
nodes.notes: CRM field names are mapped once, here. Required fields, email format, amount and currency are checked before anything moves.

nodes.name: 3 - Record Passes Validation?
3b - Park It in Needs Review With the Failing Field
nodes.notes: Bad data never reaches QuickBooks or the ops base. Someone fixes the field and replays it.

parameters.query:
INSERT INTO sync_ledger (event_id, crm, deal_id, execution_id, payload, status, claimed_at)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5::jsonb, 'claimed', now())
ON CONFLICT (event_id) DO NOTHING
RETURNING event_id, deal_id, true AS claimed;

nodes.name: 4 - Sync Ledger: Claim This Event Id Once
nodes.notes: Unique key on the event id. A resent webhook inserts nothing, and the raw payload is kept for replay.

nodes.name: 5 - Only New Events Continue
nodes.notes: A repeat delivery stops here, so no invoice or ops record is ever created twice.

nodes.name: 6 - Acknowledge the CRM Right Away
nodes.notes: Answer first, work after. A slow answer is what makes a CRM resend.

options.systemMessage: You turn one closed-won CRM deal into what each connected system needs. Clean the company name for display, read the plan text into a QuickBooks item and billing schedule, and write a two sentence summary for the team. Never invent or change an id, email or amount. If something needed is missing or unclear, set needs_review to true and name the field.

nodes.name: 7 - Claude Maps and Enriches the Record
nodes.notes: Judgment work only: clean names, read the plan terms, write the summary. Ids, emails and amounts pass straight through.

10b - Back Off 30 Seconds, Then Retry
nodes.notes: Rate limits and token refreshes are usually temporary, so it waits and tries again. Past the retry cap, the error path takes over.

nodes.name: 12 - HubSpot or Your CRM: Write Ids and Sync Status to the Deal
nodes.notes: Only the sync fields are written, so the write-back can never retrigger this workflow.

parameters.query:
UPDATE sync_ledger
SET status = 'synced', airtable_record_id = $2, quickbooks_invoice_id = $3, synced_at = now()
WHERE event_id = $1
RETURNING *;

nodes.name: 13 - Sync Ledger: Mark Done With Every Id
14 - Any Node Fails, Anywhere

parameters.query:
UPDATE sync_ledger
SET status = 'failed', failed_step = $2, error = $3, failed_at = now()
WHERE execution_id = $1
RETURNING event_id, deal_id, failed_step, error;
